_: Vendored-file manifest for oc-vendor-drift (issue #700). Each entry names a file this repo carries a copy of, the upstream revision it was flattened from, and the ONLY differences permitted. A delta entry matches OUR form via `match` and THEIR form via `match_upstream` (defaulting to `match`), because a delta line must be droppable from both sides or the comparison shifts. Anything else is drift and fails the guard.

vendor.why: The Open Questions register. This fleet's file must be named oc-questions (the vpn backend resolver globs */oc-questions and requires exactly one match); upstream names it questions. Re-flattened 2026-10-06 at origin/main 7ead63d (which carries #762 — `resolve_lane` prefers a `topic_edited` rename row over the stale creation-time `topic_name`, and the selftest covers it); before that 2026-10-05 at origin/main 657a7cb; the content last changed upstream at 657a7cb (#736 — the `--help` synopsis now names the sanctioned recommendation form `[--recommended <0-based-index|LABEL|LETTER>]` on BOTH `ask` and `amend`; the resolver was already correct and is untouched) and before that at a484af7 (#709 — `--schema` is DERIVED from FLAG_SPEC, the ONE flag table the handlers themselves parse with, so a consumer reads the contract instead of keeping a second copy that drifts; every cmd_* now parses via flag_spec(<verb>), behaviour-identical by construction) and this copy carries it byte-for-byte after the seven declared deltas. Six of the seven were UPSTREAM-IDENTICAL at the 2026-10-06 flatten (upstream had adopted them since the old ref), so they matched on both sides and stayed declared no-ops, kept so the comparison stays symmetric; the routing-default comment left that class on 2026-10-08, when the owner re-scoped the fork into a third stream; that re-scope was SUPERSEDED on 2026-10-09 (fork = the single binary-issue home, upstream PRs-only), and the local comment now reads 'two-stream routing, SKILL.md; owner order 2026-10-03, superseded 2026-10-09'. It is a live delta of TWO single-line alternatives, with `match` naming OUR forms and `match_upstream` theirs. RE-FLATTENED 2026-10-17 at origin/main a67a7dd (recorded ref was 7ead63d): upstream adopted the #494 behaviour this copy had carried LOCALLY since 2026-10-16 (the status-based DELIVERY population, DELIVERABLE_STATUSES, and the retraction-clears-the-answer legs), so the local divergence became upstream's own code and the copy is now byte-identical to a67a7dd after EIGHT declared deltas -- the six live ones above, the close-reason entry (now a symmetric no-op because upstream adopted its local form; kept so the comparison stays symmetric) and the two documentation-pointer comment lines that the old ref never compared. The ROUTING-COMMENT delta was REMOVED at the same flatten: upstream adopted our two-line form verbatim, so the entry became ASYMMETRIC -- it still stripped our two lines while its stale `match_upstream` (`# fork.`) stripped nothing upstream, shifting the comparison and reporting DRIFTED at line 202 with `6314 vendored vs 6316 upstream`. A delta whose two sides have converged must be deleted, not left declared: a one-sided strip is a defect in the comparison, not a no-op. Between 7ead63d and a67a7dd TEMPLATE/tools/questions moved +286/-24; the renderer is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the same range, so its ref is bumped for a single flatten instant, not because its content moved.

delta.why: Deployment name: derives from the invoked program so the unified-log 'tool' field and every die() remedy name the command that actually exists here. Upstream ask: the same one line.
Sibling renderer name, derived so it follows PROG. Upstream ask: the same one line.
The usage header must name the invoked program, not a hardcoded one, or --help prints a command this fleet does not have. Upstream ask: the same one line.

Fleet actor contract (#749): tools/lib/oc-log.sh resolves the log actor as OC_ACTOR first, falling back to OPENCRABS_SESSION_ID -- and the owner rule of 2026-08-30 requires every oc-* invocation to set OC_ACTOR. This copy read the session id ALONE, so every such caller was logged as actor="unknown" and could not be traced to a lane. Upstream ask: the same one line.

The C6 mechanical-closure probe's default tracker. A factory question's work unit is filed on the FACTORY tracker, so probing the fork for it answers about a repo that unit is not filed on -- a confident, WRONG 'still open'. Defaults to the factory tracker; OC_QUESTIONS_TRACKER still overrides. (The fork is a real tracker again since the 2026-10-08 re-scope, but only for FORK-ONLY defects -- never the default for a factory question.) UPSTREAM ASK: flip the same default in TEMPLATE/tools/questions.

Close REASON: it hardcoded the word 'fork' while the probe now asks the factory tracker, so the message a lane reads would name the wrong repo. Interpolating the constant makes the reason state its own scope -- '<slug>#N is CLOSED' (rule: a number travels with its predicate and scope). UPSTREAM ASK: same fix in TEMPLATE/tools/questions.

delta.match_upstream: ^# rc vocabulary, printed by --help: 0 ok / 1 finding-or-not-found /$
delta.why: Documentation pointer: this fleet keeps the rc vocabulary in tools/docs/RC-CONTRACT.md and the comment names that home; upstream keeps it inline in --help. Behaviour-identical (a comment), but it is a real byte difference and it was UNDECLARED until 2026-10-17, when the re-flatten to a67a7dd surfaced it as drift (measured: the only two undeclared lines in the 14-line diff). UPSTREAM ASK: none -- upstream's form is correct for upstream.

delta.match_upstream: ^# Unified tools log \(entry: ts, tool, actor, args, exit, secs, extra\)$
delta.why: Same class as the rc-vocabulary line: this fleet points at RC-CONTRACT.md for the unified-log schema instead of restating the field list, so the two copies cannot drift apart on a schema the doc already owns. Undeclared until the 2026-10-17 re-flatten surfaced it. UPSTREAM ASK: none.

vendor.why: The json-render catalog the register renders its page through. Re-flattened 2026-10-06 at origin/main 7ead63d; the only upstream movement since ece0f4e is commit 6bc92ae (fix(template): no shipped file depends on the absent `oc-*` toolchain, #85), which genericised the two header comment lines so upstream names its own `questions` / `tools/questions`. Those names are WRONG for this fleet -- the copy here really is `tools/state/oc-questions-render.mjs`, invoked by `tools/state/oc-questions` -- so both lines are declared deltas, same class as the register's deployment-name deltas. Otherwise byte-identical.

delta.match: ^// oc\-questions\-render\.mjs — the Open Questions page renderer \(#547\)\.$
delta.match_upstream: ^// questions\-render\.mjs — the Open Questions page renderer \(#547\)\.$
delta.why: Self-identification header: must name the file that exists here. Upstream names its own TEMPLATE file.

delta.match: ^// VERSIONED SOURCE\. tools/state/oc\-questions copies this file into the build directory$
delta.match_upstream: ^// VERSIONED SOURCE\. tools/questions copies this file into the build directory$
delta.why: Names the invoker: ours is tools/state/oc-questions, upstream's is tools/questions. A genericised name here would mislead.
